title: Species-dependent pair coupling at separation 5: A attracts B, A repels C, both at rest

claims.statement: Two particles at rest, separation 5.0 along a line, one species A and one species B, accelerate toward each other with per-particle magnitudes K_A(B) = 9.0 (on A) and K_B(A) = 12.3 (on B), in units of 1/r^2.5 at r = 5 (chamber and time units). Repeated in 2026-11-18/r1/lab-a/001 and 002 (agreement 4%), each consistent with the predictor at tracker noise (residual rms 0.049-0.053 per coordinate, no census events over T = 2). For comparison, two A at the same separation accelerate with K_A(A) = 18.0 (P-0003 runs). The A-on-B and B-on-A values are not equal; the ratio K_B/K_A = 1.37 is what momentum conservation requires if m_B/m_A = 0.73. No claim is made about masses. Constants are fit to these runs; the prediction test is the B-C pair (2026-11-18/r2/lab-a/001-002, round 2).

Two particles at rest, separation 5.0 along a line, one species A and one species C, REPEL: A is accelerated away from C with K_A(C) = -8.6 and C away from A with K_C(A) = -21.4 (same units). Single run 2026-11-18/r1/lab-a/005; the raw displacements at t = 2 (A moves 0.29 away, C moves 0.76 away) are many times the tracker noise, and the predictor fits the run at noise level (rms 0.048 per coordinate, no census events). This is a single-run claim; the sign is firm, the magnitudes need the repeat (2026-11-18/r2/lab-a/005) before they are trusted.
